_README: TEMPLATE for the owner-only half of the training charter (#5087). Copy to config/training_charter.private.local.json (gitignored) and fill it, or put the same object in env TRAINING_CHARTER_PRIVATE_JSON, or at the owner-private S3 key config/coaching/training_charter.private.json. The repo is PUBLIC: no real value ever goes in a tracked file. lambdas/training/training_charter.py merges this over the public config/training_charter.json and reports private_loaded + private_keys; nothing under these keys is ever on the PUBLISHED_WHITELIST. anchor_foods (#5103) is the weekly menu's anchor-food table: one row per food with a stable id, the label and serving as the owner writes them, the label values per serving (kcal, protein_g, carb_g, fat_g, fibre_g), an optional max_per_day (replaces the charter's default per-food cap for that row), off_limits true to keep a food off the menu, the package it is bought in (servings per package) for the grocery list, and an optional section (the store aisle the grocery list groups it under, e.g. produce; blank = other, #5104); health.weekly_menu reads it. Optional food-quality tags (#5105, read by health.food_quality): fatty_fish true marks a fatty-fish food (the charter's nutrition.food_quality.fatty_fish weekly range counts its servings; the fibre per serving is the row's fibre_g), and nutrient_tags is a list of short words the lab-driven priorities row can name (the week's servings of those foods are reported beside it). fixed_meals (#5103, owner ruling 2026-10-26) is the list of fixed feedings the weekly menu plans around (the meal-service dinner): one row per fixed feeding with a stable id, the label as the owner writes it, the slot it sits in (dinner = the day's last feeding, breakfast = its first), the label values (kcal, protein_g, carb_g, fat_g; fibre_g may stay null = unknown, counted as none), days = the weekday names it applies to (e.g. Monday ... Sunday), and source (free text, where the values were read); health.weekly_menu subtracts it from the day's band and floors, counts it as one feeding and fits the anchors into the rest. No key or an empty list = no fixed feeding; an unreadable row refuses the menu.
